clause-reference-back-on-a-shipped-strin.why: Owner decision 151 ruling 2-أ deletes «البند N» / «الجزء N» from the seven strings that cited one of OUR OWN documents: the reader has nowhere to look that clause up. `check:process-prefix` carries the rule at budget zero and must name this file and line. ⚠️ The span is MID-SENTENCE, which is the shape an anchored matcher would miss — five of the seven were like this.

one-word-changed-in-her-ratified-arabic.why: Decision 151 §٤ row 2 ratifies «لوحة الالتزام». `decision-151.strings.test.ts` re-slices annex §٧ at test time and compares byte for byte, so changing ONE word must kill it by name — and must NOT be caught by the two gates above, which are about clause references and digits.

paid-declaration-left-behind-as-stale.why: Decision 146 ruling 6-a paid this debt, so the declaration row was deleted in the same commit. Putting it back must fail the gate's STALE direction — a declared string that no longer occurs. Without that direction a paid debt could sit on the list for ever and nobody would know the word had arrived.
